chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: Songwriting credits in Ellington's music
summary: Royal doubts who wrote what, noting Irving Mills's name is on much of Duke's work.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did Harry Carney write any part of it? I know he's got a credit on it, but I (inaudible). I've heard...
I think Lawrence or somebody said --
-- that Duke gave him a writing credit, but I (inaudible) think
-- they said that he didn't write it.
But it sort of grew, is that it, through the years?
I don't know anything about it.

I haven't got the slightest idea. Nope. That was all inside stuff, the writing and a whole lot of things, a whole lot of people have been given credit for the writing of things, down through the years, that had nothing absolutely to do with the writing.
There were some who wrote and didn't get credit.
Irving Mills' (PHONETIC) name is on half of Duke Ellington's records as writer and Irving never wrote a note in his life. he was the manager.
That's right. So, all those things, you just have to take them with a grain of salt and just figure out who actually did write them and take it or give it. It makes no difference.
